name: Myelodysplastic Syndromes
remarks: Myelodysplastic Syndromes (MDS) — Comprehensive Synthea Module
Version: 2.0 | Audit-corrected
Based on: WHO 5th Edition 2022, ICC 2022, IPSS-R, IPSS-M,
NCCN Guidelines v1.2026, ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines,
ASH Blood 2023 treatment review (Hellström-Lindberg & Kröger).
Epidemiology:
- Incidence: ~4 per 100,000 persons/year overall; 26.1 per 100,000 in age ≥65.
- Median age at diagnosis: 70–77 years. More common in males (~1.5-2x).
- ~25% of patients progress to AML over their disease course.
- Median overall survival: ~3 years (range: months to >8 years by subtype).
WHO 2022 Subtypes modelled (8 subtypes):
1. MDS with low blasts, single lineage dysplasia (MDS-LB-SLD)     — ~15%
2. MDS with low blasts, multilineage dysplasia (MDS-LB-MLD)       — ~25%
3. MDS with mutated SF3B1 (MDS-SF3B1; formerly MDS-RS)            — ~10%
4. MDS with isolated del(5q) (MDS-5q)                             — ~5%
5. MDS, hypoplastic (MDS-h)                                       — ~5%
6. MDS with biallelic TP53 inactivation (MDS-biTP53)              — ~5%
7. MDS with increased blasts-1 (MDS-IB1, 5-9% BM blasts)         — ~17%
8. MDS with increased blasts-2 (MDS-IB2, 10-19% BM blasts)       — ~18%
Distributions sum to 1.0.
Risk stratification: IPSS-R — very low / low / intermediate / high / very high.
MDS-LB-SLD / MDS-SF3B1 / MDS-5q / MDS-h → lower risk
MDS-LB-MLD → lower risk (intermediate IPSS-R in some)
MDS-biTP53 / MDS-IB1 / MDS-IB2 → higher risk
Treatment pathways modelled:
Lower-risk: watchful waiting, ESA-gated by EPO level (epoetin alfa if EPO≤500),
IST (ATG+cyclosporine if EPO>500 or hypocellular MDS-h),
luspatercept (MDS-SF3B1 subtype only), lenalidomide (MDS-5q only),
imetelstat (ESA-refractory), iron chelation (deferasirox),
RBC transfusions.
Higher-risk: azacitidine (HMA first-line), decitabine,
venetoclax+HMA (second-line), IDH inhibitors (IDH1/2 mutated),
intensive chemotherapy (3+7; fit young patients),
allogeneic stem cell transplantation (allo-SCT).
MDS-biTP53: HMA ± venetoclax; SCT if feasible; very poor prognosis.
Outcomes: stable disease, haematological improvement, AML transformation, death.
Coding references:
SNOMED-CT codes: IHTSDO SNOMED CT Browser
RxNorm codes: NLM RxNorm Browser
LOINC codes: LOINC.org

SNOMED-CT 234326001 = Bone marrow biopsy (procedure).
Mandatory for MDS diagnosis.
Assesses: dysplasia (≥10% per lineage), blast %, ring sideroblasts, cellularity.
MDS-h: cellularity <25% (or <50% for age) required for hypoplastic subtype.

SNOMED-CT 405825005 = Cytogenetic analysis (procedure).
Mandatory karyotyping for IPSS-R risk scoring and subtype classification.
Key cytogenetic abnormalities:
Favourable: del(5q) isolated, del(12p), del(20q), -Y, del(11q)
Intermediate: +8, del(7q), i(17q), +19, any other single abnormality
Poor: -7, inv(3)/t(3;3), del(3q), -7/del(7q)+1 other, complex (<3 abnormalities)
Very poor: complex karyotype (≥3 abnormalities)
Molecular NGS panel (30+ genes): TET2, SF3B1, ASXL1, SRSF2, DNMT3A, RUNX1,
TP53 (key for biTP53 subtype), IDH1/2, EZH2, NRAS, CBL, U2AF1, BCOR.
80–90% of MDS patients carry ≥1 somatic mutation.

Epoetin alfa (Procrit / Epogen) — ESA first-line for lower-risk MDS with anaemia.
RxNorm 1237808 = epoetin alfa 40000 UNT/ML Injectable Solution.
Indication: symptomatic anaemia, EPO ≤500 mU/mL, no del(5q) and no RS ≥15%.
Dosing: 40,000–60,000 IU SC weekly; assess at 8–12 weeks.
Discontinue if no HI-E by 16 weeks (IWG 2023 criteria).
Response rate: ~40–60% if EPO ≤500 mU/mL (Nordic Score).
Darbepoetin alfa (300 mcg SC q3w) is an equivalent alternative.
ESA response assessment at 8–16 weeks.
IWG 2023 HI-E definition: Hb increase ≥1.5 g/dL or transfusion independence ≥8 weeks.
ESA response in lower-risk MDS (EPO ≤500 mU/mL cohort):
~40–60% achieve HI-E (haematological improvement — erythroid lineage).
Median response duration: 18–24 months.
Failure → luspatercept (if SF3B1), imetelstat, lenalidomide, or transfusions.

Luspatercept-aamt (Reblozyl) — TGF-β superfamily ligand trap.
RxNorm 2200671 = luspatercept-aamt 25 MG/ML Injectable Solution.
FDA approved August 2020: ESA-refractory/ineligible MDS-RS (MEDALIST trial).
FDA expanded Feb 2023 (COMMANDS trial): first-line in ESA-naive lower-risk MDS.
Dosing: 1.0 mg/kg SC q3 weeks; titrate to 1.33 or 1.75 mg/kg if needed.
MEDALIST: 38% TI rate vs 13% placebo (≥8 weeks at 24 weeks).
COMMANDS: superior TI rate vs epoetin alfa (58.5% vs 31.2% at week 24).
FIX 7: Only prescribed to MDS-SF3B1 patients in this module.
MEDALIST first-line response: ~38% TI rate at 24 weeks.
COMMANDS first-line: ~58% TI rate (MDS-SF3B1 enriched).
Using intermediate estimate (~45%) for mixed first- and second-line population.

Lenalidomide (Revlimid) — immunomodulatory drug.
RxNorm 602725 = lenalidomide 10 MG Oral Capsule.
FDA approved: lower-risk MDS with del(5q) and transfusion-dependent anaemia.
Dosing: 10 mg/day PO for 21/28 days; adjust for renal function.
MDS-003 trial: ~67% TI; ~45% cytogenetic response.
Screen for TP53 mutation before starting: co-mutation → AML risk with lenalidomide.
Requires REMS enrolment (RevAssist programme — teratogenicity).
AML transformation on lenalidomide (TP53 co-mutated del5q): up to 25–30%.
MDS-5q response to lenalidomide: ~67% TI rate (MDS-003 trial).
FIX 9: del5q-specific AML transformation ~5% even with lenalidomide response.
Median lenalidomide response duration in del(5q): ~2 years.
Progression invariably occurs; TP53 mutations drive lenalidomide resistance.
Imetelstat (Rytelo) — first-in-class oligonucleotide telomerase inhibitor.
RxNorm 2638073 = imetelstat 47 MG/ML Injectable Solution.
FDA approved June 6 2024: lower-risk MDS relapsed/refractory to ESA.
IMerge Phase 3 (Lancet 2024): 40% TI ≥8 weeks vs 15% placebo (p<0.001).
Median TI duration in responders: 51.6 weeks.
Dosing: 7.1 mg/kg IV over 2 hours every 4 weeks.
Key toxicities: grade 3/4 cytopaenias (neutropaenia 68%, thrombocytopaenia 65%).
Requires CBC monitoring; dose delays common.
Not approved in higher-risk MDS (IMerge studied lower-risk ESA-refractory patients).
IMerge Phase 3 (ESA-refractory lower-risk MDS): 40% TI rate.
Median TI duration in IMerge responders: ~52 weeks.
Anti-thymocyte globulin (horse ATG, Atgam) — immunosuppressive therapy (IST).
RxNorm 205460 = antithymocyte globulin (equine) 50 MG/ML Injectable Solution.
Indications (NCCN): EPO >500 mU/mL, or MDS-h regardless of EPO level,
younger patients (<60), HLA-DR15+, PNH clone positivity, STAT3-mutant T-cells,
BM blasts ≤5%, short disease duration.
Dosing: 40 mg/kg/day IV × 4 days (horse ATG) with supportive care.
Combined with cyclosporine (see below).
Response rate: ~30–35% HI. Relapse rate ~30% at 3 years.
Rabbit ATG (thymoglobulin) is less effective in MDS than horse ATG.

Deferasirox (Exjade / Jadenu) — oral iron chelator.

FDA/EMA approved for transfusional iron overload in MDS.
Dosing: 20 mg/kg/day PO dispersible (Exjade) or 14 mg/kg/day film-coated (Jadenu).
Monitor: renal function (SCr, eGFR), LFTs, CBC monthly.
Target: ferritin <1000 ng/mL; discontinue at ferritin <500 ng/mL.

Azacitidine (Vidaza) — hypomethylating agent (HMA); first-line for higher-risk MDS.
RxNorm 278177 = azacitidine 100 MG Injection.
FDA approved 2004; EMA approved 2008.
AZA-001 trial: OS advantage vs conventional care (24.5 vs 15 months median OS).
Dosing: 75 mg/m² SC/IV daily × 7 days every 28 days.
Overall response rate: ~50% (CR ~17%, PR ~12%, HI ~21%).
Assess response after ≥4–6 cycles (minimum); continue until progression.
Oral azacitidine (CC-486) approved for AML maintenance — not for MDS.
Decitabine (Dacogen) — alternative HMA for higher-risk MDS.
RxNorm 583214 = decitabine 50 MG Injection.
FDA approved 2006. ADOPT trial: ~17–26% ORR.
Dosing: 20 mg/m² IV × 5 days q28 days (most common).
Oral decitabine + cedazuridine (Inqovi) FDA approved 2020 — bioequivalent to IV.
Similar efficacy to azacitidine; centre/patient preference drives selection.
Minimum 4–6 cycles (4–6 months) to assess HMA response.

Cytarabine — cornerstone of intensive '3+7' induction for higher-risk MDS.
RxNorm 28648 = cytarabine 20 MG/ML Injectable Solution.
Regimen: cytarabine 100–200 mg/m² continuous IV infusion × 7 days
+ idarubicin 12 mg/m²/day IV × 3 days.
Used in younger (<65–70), fit patients with good/intermediate cytogenetics.
CR rate for MDS with excess blasts (AML-like induction): ~40–50%.
Bridge to allo-SCT if CR achieved.
NOT appropriate for: MDS-biTP53, monosomal karyotype, TP53 single-hit, ECOG ≥2.
Significant morbidity: prolonged BM aplasia (4–6 weeks), febrile neutropaenia,
mucositis, organ toxicity.
Idarubicin — anthracycline component of '3+7' induction.
RxNorm 25463 = idarubicin hydrochloride 5 MG/ML Injectable Solution.
Dosing: 12 mg/m²/day IV × 3 days (concurrent with cytarabine).
Daunorubicin (60 mg/m²/day × 3 days) is an acceptable alternative.
Liposomal formulations available for elderly/cardiac-risk patients.
BM recovery and CR assessment: ~4–8 weeks post-induction.
Second induction cycle if residual blasts at day 14 BM assessment.

Fluoroquinolone + antifungal prophylaxis if ANC <0.5.
Symptom management, QoL optimisation.
